'''Richard Joel Wassersug''' (born April 13, 1946) was an Honorary [[professor]] in the Department of Cellular and Physiological Sciences at the [[University of British Columbia]]. He was also an adjunct professor in the Department of Medical Neuroscience at [[Dalhousie University]] with a cross appointment in the Department of [[Psychology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://anatomy.medicine.dal.ca/deptmembs.htm |title=Dalhousie Anatomy and Neurobiology Faculty and Administration |publisher=Anatomy.medicine.dal.ca |accessdate=2011-03-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://psychology.dal.ca/People/Cross-Appointed_Facu.php |title=Cross-Appointed Faculty - Department of Psychology |publisher=Psychology.dal.ca |date=2010-10-14 |accessdate=2011-03-12}}</ref> In addition, he is an adjunct professor at The Australian Research Centre in Sex, Health & Society (ARCSHS), [[La Trobe University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.latrobe.edu.au/arcshs/research-profiles/view-profile?uname=RWassersug |title=Staff profile, La Trobe University |publisher=Latrobe.edu.au |date=2010-08-12 |accessdate=2011-03-12}}</ref>

==Biography==

Wassersug received his [[Bachelor of Arts]] from [[Tufts University]] in [[geology]] and biology in 1967 and his [[PhD]] from the [[University of Chicago]] in [[Evolutionary Biology]] in 1973. He became a professor in the Dalhousie University’s Department of Anatomy and Neurobiology in 1986 and Honorary Associate Professor in Dalhousie University’s School of Physiotherapy in 1989. In 2010 he was an honorary visiting professor at the Australian Research Centre in Sex, Health and Society, at La Trobe University.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://anatomy.medicine.dal.ca/Wassersug/currentresearch.html|title=Department of Medical Neuroscience}}</ref>{{self-published inline|date=November 2010}}

Wassersug is an outspoken communicator of scientific ideas, having served on [[CBC Radio]]’s Maritime Noon Science Panel and as a columnist on The Canadian Discovery Channel's [[Daily Planet (TV series)]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbc.ca/maritimenoon/phone-in-regulars.html |title=Maritime Noon &#124; Phone-In Regulars |publisher=CBC.ca |date=2009-06-25 |accessdate=2011-03-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Ingram |first=Jay |year=2010 |title=Daily Planet: The Ultimate Book of Everyday Science |publisher=Penguin Canada |page=145 |isbn=978-0-14-317786-9}}</ref>

==Research==

The majority of his scientific career has been spent studying the functional [[morphology (biology)|morphology]] and behavior of [[anuran]] [[larvae]]. He has published over 150 peer-reviewed papers on these animals. Wassersug’s more recent work focuses on [[prostate cancer]] and the psychology of [[androgen]] deprivation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://anatomy.medicine.dal.ca/wassersug/currentresearch.html|title=Department of Medical Neuroscience}}</ref>{{self-published inline|date=November 2010}} His book ''Androgen Deprivation Therapy: an essential guide for prostate cancer patients and their loved ones'' (Demos Health) has been through three editions (2014, 2021, 2023).

Wassersug has received funding for his research from the [[Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council]], the [[Canadian Institutes of Health Research]], Prostate Cancer Canada, the Prostate Cancer Foundation of British Columbia, Nova Scotia Health Research Foundation, the [[Canadian Space Agency]], [[Parks Canada]], and the Dalhousie Medical Research Foundation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://anatomy.medicine.dal.ca/wassersug/RichardWassersugCV.html|title=Department of Medical Neuroscience}}</ref>{{self-published inline|date=November 2010}}

==Awards==

Wassersug received the Science Communication Award from the [[Atlantic Provinces]] Council on the Sciences in 2001.<ref>Atlantic Provinces Council on the Sciences
Biennial Report April 1, 2001 – March 31, 2003 http://apics.dal.ca/members/Biennial%20Report%20Apr01-Mar03.pdf</ref> He was also named a Science Champion during the Discovery Awards for Science and Technology in 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dalnews.dal.ca/2002/12/11/people.shtml |title=People |publisher=dalnews.dal.ca |date=2002-12-11 |accessdate=2011-03-12}}</ref>

He won an [[Ig Nobel Prize]] in 2000 for his firsthand report, "On the Comparative Palatability of Some Dry-Season [[Tadpoles]] from [[Costa Rica]]".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://improbable.com/ig/winners/#ig2000|title = Past Ig Winners|date = August 2006}}</ref>
